architecture.mechanism: In a cooling-plate-cooled battery pack, the cooling plate acts as a thermal channel that conducts high temperatures between modules, making thermal runaway propagation consistently severe at pack level, while added thermal insulation (intended to contain heat) instead produces wider-spread higher temperatures.
architecture.intervention: Replace the single continuous cooling plate with module-segmented cooling loops separated by thermal breaks (low-conductivity isolation barriers between adjacent module cooling segments) so each module is cooled without a continuous high-conductivity path for heat to travel between modules.
architecture.expected_effect: A thermal runaway event triggered in one module is contained locally rather than propagating to adjacent modules, preventing pack-level cascading failure and the associated electrical faults that can disable vehicle systems and illuminate ABS, ESC, and check engine warning indicators.
architecture.falsification_test: Initiate thermal runaway in one module of an instrumented pack prototype (nail penetration or overcharge abuse test) with thermocouples on adjacent modules, and compare the continuous cooling plate design against the segmented design; the mechanism is falsified if adjacent modules reach thermal runaway onset temperature at statistically similar times in both designs.
